1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 0.5 ul is below what the p20_single_gen2 can measure (1 ul at least)
   line 68:  p20.aspirate(0.5, polymerase_well)
   At line 68 the p20_single_gen2 is asked to draw 0.5 ul, below its minimum of 1 ul (this
   line did it 12 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong
   amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator
   passes the move. Wells: well C2 in slot 2.
   Affected: well C2 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [dea5941dd02f]

2. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well C2 in slot 2: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 68:  p20.aspirate(0.5, polymerase_well)
   At line 68 the p20_single_gen2 draws 0.5 ul from polymerase (well C2 in slot 2) with its
   tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 4 ul, which in this
   Opentrons 24 Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap reaches only 0.89 mm up: the
   tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 8 times, after 4 times in the
   liquid; 4 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the
   liquid. The 8 wells filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well C2 in slot 2.
   Also reached 8 other wells: wells A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11 and A12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 6 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error

5. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was loaded but never set
   line 65:  p20.aspirate(10, buffer_well)
   At line 65 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 9 more in slot
   2, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at
   room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), fwd primer
   (reagent), polymerase (reagent), rev primer (reagent) and 13 more sat on a block that was
   never cold; the robot pipetted there 72 times over the run. The person setting up the
   deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2
   and 9 more in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 9 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24
   Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 2, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at
   the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html

6. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: buffer (well C1 in slot 2)
   line 65:  p20.aspirate(10, buffer_well)
   At line 65 the tip went into buffer (well C1 in slot 2) while it still carried polymerase
   (well C2 in slot 2), fwd primer (well C3 in slot 2), rev primer (well C4 in slot 2) and
   water (well C5 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves
   a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does
   not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 8 other
   wells: wells A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11 and A12 in slot 3.
   Affected: well C1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 8 other wells: wells A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11 and A12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 65 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: 0.5 ul is below what the p20_single_gen2 can measure (1 ul at least)
findings.explanation: At line 68 the p20_single_gen2 is asked to draw 0.5 ul, below its minimum of 1 ul (this line did it 12 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: well C2 in slot 2.
findings.fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well C2 in slot 2: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 68 the p20_single_gen2 draws 0.5 ul from polymerase (well C2 in slot 2) with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 4 ul, which in this Opentrons 24 Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap reaches only 0.89 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 8 times, after 4 times in the liquid; 4 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 8 wells filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 6 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.

findings.title: A temperature module was loaded but never set
findings.explanation: At line 65 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 9 more in slot 2, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), fwd primer (reagent), polymerase (reagent), rev primer (reagent) and 13 more sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 72 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 9 more in slot 2.
findings.fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24 Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 2, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: buffer (well C1 in slot 2)
findings.explanation: At line 65 the tip went into buffer (well C1 in slot 2) while it still carried polymerase (well C2 in slot 2), fwd primer (well C3 in slot 2), rev primer (well C4 in slot 2) and water (well C5 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 8 other wells: wells A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11 and A12 in slot 3.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 65 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.
